title: feat(plugin-auth): mobile sign-in hand-off over better-auth's one-time-token plugin, bound to the shell's PKCE challenge
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-warren"} -->
_Requested by **Warren** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ8?thread=cmsg_01U5RdnAAmkSQmZbqh6FtqZ88qZwSN6JGUwLRFTsXeHxbV)_
Fixes #29714

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

Clause-② is `yes (widening)` because three auth routes become reachable that were 404 on `main`: the ObjectStack hand-off and the vendor plugin's generate and verify. Nothing an author writes changes, so `Metadata-protocol: none`. The spec half (route paths, the request shapes, and the `trustedAppSchemes` key) is #29736, and **this PR stays draft until #29736 lands**.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：plugin-auth 开启 better-auth 自带的 one-time-token 插件，加一个 `GET /one-time-token/handoff` 路由：系统浏览器里登录后，把会话以一次性、一分钟有效的令牌交给已注册的 app scheme，App 在 `/one-time-token/verify` 兑换。
- 为什么改：Google 等身份提供方拒绝在内嵌 WebView 里登录，移动端用这类账号目前登录不了（裁决 B：复用插件，不手写兑换端点）。
- 风险与回滚：这是认证边界。令牌存储键绑定了壳生成的 PKCE challenge，截获回调的其他 App 兑换不了，也烧不掉正主的令牌；生成路由对客户端请求一律拒绝。只在部署配置了 `trustedAppSchemes` 时才挂载插件，回滚即删掉该配置或回退本 PR。an intercepted callback cannot be redeemed」证明截获的令牌被拒且正主随后仍能兑换，「ruling A
- 先看：`one-time-token-handoff.ts`（顶部注释是拦截论证，`oneTimeTokenStoreHasher`）；`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` 新增的插件块；`auth-plugin.ts` 的 handoff 挂载。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/one-time-token-handoff.test.ts`，预期 39/39 通过，其中「an intercepted callback cannot be redeemed」证明截获的令牌被拒且正主随后仍能兑换，「ruling A」一组证明超过五分钟的会话和跨站导航被拒。
- 需要你做的：遗留风险一已按你的裁决 A（[6597001931](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/29714#issuecomment-6597001931)）实现；请在座位审完后审合本 PR。

## What changes

**The flow** (the mobile card designs the shell half; this PR is the server half):

1. The shell makes an RFC 7636 `code_verifier` and keeps it.
2. In the system auth session (`ASWebAuthenticationSession`, Custom Tabs), after a sign-in there, the shell opens `GET /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/handoff?redirect_uri=SCHEME://PATH&code_challenge=C&code_challenge_method=S256`, where `C = BASE64URL(SHA-256(code_verifier))`.
3. The route checks that the scheme is registered, mints a token from the signed-in session through the vendor plugin's own generate endpoint (called in-process), and answers `302` to `redirect_uri` with `token=T` added (`Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; the shell's own query, such as `state`, is kept).
4. The shell, or the Console it hands both values to, redeems at the vendor route `POST /api/v1/auth/one-time-token/verify` with `{ "token": "T.code_verifier" }` and receives the vendor `{ session, user }` and the session cookie.

**The plugin**, `oneTimeToken({ expiresIn: 1, disableClientRequest: true, storeToken: { type: 'custom-hasher', hash } })`, added through `addOptionalPlugin` ahead of the custom session, mounted only when `trustedAppSchemes` registers at least one scheme.

- **Hashed storage.** The stored identifier is `one-time-token:` plus a SHA-256 key; neither the token nor the challenge is in the row.
- **Expiry: 1 minute** (the vendor default is 3). The token travels by a redirect the operating system delivers at once and is redeemed by the app's next request, so a minute is generous even on a slow device, and every second beyond that is only time for a stolen token to be tried.
- **Generation is server-side only.** `disableClientRequest` refuses every HTTP request to `/one-time-token/generate` (400 with a session, 401 without). The hand-off calls `auth.api.generateOneTimeToken({ headers })`, which carries no request, so it passes.

**How an intercepted callback cannot be redeemed.** The vendor plugin by itself is not bound to the attempt that started the sign-in: whoever holds `T` redeems it, and on a phone another app can register the same custom scheme and receive the callback. The binding uses only the plugin's published `storeToken` option:

- At generation, the hand-off runs the vendor generate inside an `AsyncLocalStorage` scope that holds `C`, and the custom hasher stores the session under `SHA-256(T ":" C)`.
- At redemption, there is no scope, so the hasher reads the body's token as `T.code_verifier` (the vendor alphabet for `T` has no `.`, so the first `.` is the separator) and looks up `SHA-256(T ":" S256(code_verifier))`.
- An interceptor holds `T` alone. `T`, `T.`, `T` with a guessed verifier, or `T` with the challenge itself all hash to a key no row has, so the vendor answers its own `400 Invalid token`. Because the lookup used the wrong key, nothing is consumed and the shell that started the hand-off still redeems. The verifier never leaves the device; only its hash travels, in step 2.
- A token minted server-side outside the hand-off's scope is stored under a key no redemption can reach, so it fails closed.

**The registered-scheme list** is the spec's `AuthConfig.trustedAppSchemes` (#29736, beside `trustedOrigins`); there is no local declaration. Each entry is checked by the spec's own `TrustedAppSchemeSchema`, imported into `appSchemeRefusal` and never copied, because the auth manager also receives plain objects that never passed `AuthConfigSchema`: lowercase reverse-domain private-use schemes with no `:` suffix and no empty or trailing label (RFC 8252 §7.1, for example `com.example.app`; `com..app` and `com.example.` are refused). `http`, `https`, `javascript`, `data`, `file`, `blob`, `about`, `vbscript`, `ws` and `wss` get a named "web or script scheme" refusal first; none of them contains a dot, so the schema refuses each anyway, and that check exists only for the clearer message. A bad entry fails `AuthManager` construction and `applyConfigPatch`, naming the entry; it is never dropped. A `redirect_uri` whose scheme is not registered (matched case-insensitively) answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with no `Location`, so the route is never an open redirect. The route paths `ONE_TIME_TOKEN_HANDOFF_PATH` and `ONE_TIME_TOKEN_VERIFY_PATH` derive from `AuthEndpointPaths.oneTimeTokenHandoff` / `oneTimeTokenVerify`.

**Correction to the earlier body:** it said the local scheme check applied "the same rules" as the spec. It did not: the local regex `^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$` plus "contains a dot" accepted `com..app` and `com.example.`, which the spec refuses. The import closes that gap, and the two entries are now pinned.

**The hand-off route's other answers.** It accepts a closed query set (`redirect_uri`, `code_challenge`, `code_challenge_method`, each at most once). An unknown or repeated name, a missing or relative `redirect_uri`, a missing or malformed challenge, or a method other than `S256` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before anything is minted. A signed-out caller gets `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`. The mount is unconditional: with no scheme registered, every target is refused with a 400 that says how to register one.

**The hand-off carries only a fresh sign-in (ruling A, [6597001931](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/29714#issuecomment-6597001931)).** Two refusals run before any token is minted:

1. A session whose vendor `session.createdAt` is more than five minutes old (`ONE_TIME_TOKEN_HANDOFF_SESSION_MAX_AGE_SECONDS = 300`) answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` "Sign in again…". 401 because the remedy is a sign-in, the same as having no session.
2. A request carrying `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. The header is checked only when present; `none`, `same-origin`, `same-site` and an absent header pass.

**Ledger rows.** In `auth-route-ledger.ts` (family `one-time-token`, `requires: 'oneTimeToken'`):

- `GET /one-time-token/handoff`: `objectstack`, `server-only`.
- `POST /one-time-token/verify`: `better-auth`, `public`.
- `GET /one-time-token/generate`: `better-auth`, `server-only`.

The two vendor routes are added to `BETTER_AUTH_MOUNTED_SURFACE`. The conformance suite registers one app scheme so the maximal surface carries them, and its objectstack-mount pin gains the hand-off. `check:auth-mount-ledger` accounts for all 24 mounts. No route-envelope row applies: `check:route-envelope` audits `*-routes.ts` modules and dispatcher domains, and the hand-off is a raw auth mount like its siblings, answering the shared `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }` envelope on every refusal.

## Why

Some identity providers (Google among them) refuse embedded WebViews, so a mobile user who signs in with one cannot sign in to the app today (objectstack-ai/mobile#176 detects the refusal). The maintainer ruled option B on objectstack-ai/mobile#148 (comment 6593861138, 「同意」): reuse better-auth's one-time-token plugin, with no hand-written exchange endpoint. Verify is the vendor's route, unchanged.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/one-time-token-handoff.test.ts` (39 cases) runs the real `AuthManager` (better-auth 1.7.12 and its plugin) over the package's shared in-memory engine, with the hand-off through the real `registerAuthRoutes` raw-app registration, the way `sys-session-revoke.test.ts` does.

- **Round trip.** The hand-off answers `302` to the registered scheme with `state` kept, no-store and no-referrer. The redeem returns Alice's user and a session cookie. A replay answers `400 Invalid token`.
- **Interception refusal.** `T`, `T.`, `T.` plus a guessed verifier, and `T.` plus the challenge each answer `400 Invalid token` with no cookie. The real `T.code_verifier` then answers `200`.
- **Storage.** The new `sys_verification` row's identifier holds neither `T` nor `C`, and equals the key the redemption computes.
- **Expiry.** A redeem one minute and one second later answers `400`.
- **Generate.** A client request answers `400 Client requests are disabled` with a session and `401` without. A server-side mint outside the hand-off is unredeemable.
- **Redirect target.** `com.attacker.app://`, `https://` and `javascript:` answer `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` with no `Location`. A mixed-case registered scheme matches. With no scheme registered, verify is `404` and the hand-off refuses every target. A signed-out caller gets `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`.
- **Request validation.** Seven malformed queries each answer 400 `VALIDATION_ERROR`, and generate is never called.
- **Ruling A.** A session one second past the 300-second window answers `401 UNAUTHENTICATED`, with no `Location` and no new verification row; one five seconds inside it answers `302`. `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`; `none`, `same-origin`, `same-site` and no header answer `302`.
- **`trustedAppSchemes`.** Twelve bad entries (the earlier ten plus `com..app` and `com.example.`, which the spec's schema refuses) are refused by the assertion, by construction and by `applyConfigPatch`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Residual risk 1 (an app starts its own hand-off) is closed by ruling A** ([6597001931](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/29714#issuecomment-6597001931)). The silent case, an app opening the hand-off in a system browser that has held the user's session for days, now answers 401 because the session is older than five minutes. What remains is a narrow window: an app that opens the hand-off within five minutes of the user's own sign-in in that browser.
- **The web trigger is covered by refusal 2.** The session cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, so any web page could start the hand-off with a top-level GET navigation, and on Android an app squatting the scheme would then need no user action at all. Browsers that send Fetch Metadata mark that navigation `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`, and the hand-off refuses it. A browser that sends no Fetch Metadata is not covered by this refusal and still meets refusal 1. Option B (an interstitial that POSTs) is the only design that closes the trigger in every browser, and it was not chosen.
- **Shell consequence:** posted on #29714 for the mobile filer as [6597073964](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/29714#issuecomment-6597073964); not restated here.
- **The redeemed session is the system browser's session, not a new one.** The vendor plugin stores the session token and verify returns that same session. Signing out in the app therefore also signs out the system browser, and the ADR-0069 auth gate (password change, MFA enrolment) that holds the browser session holds the app too. Nothing is widened by this, but the mobile card should know it.
- **No sign-in audit event is written for a redemption.** The after-hooks key on `/sign-in/email` and its siblings, and no session row is created, so `sys_session` and the sign-in counters do not move. Noted, not filed.
- **Signed-out hand-off answers 401 JSON**, not a redirect to the Console login. No measured Console route takes a return URL the hand-off could name, and advertising one would be the declared-not-enforced shape. The shell is expected to complete a sign-in in the auth session before opening the hand-off.
- **Order conflict, reported per os-dev:** the dispatch order asks for `pnpm lint`. os-dev's local-verification section assigns repo-wide lint to CI. I ran eslint on every touched file (exit 0) and also ran the full `pnpm lint`; its result is under Verification.

## Verification

<details><summary>Measured before and after (better-auth 1.7.12, plugin-auth on main 87956dcc, then this branch)</summary>

- Before: `GET /one-time-token/generate` anonymous answers 404, and signed in also 404. `POST /one-time-token/verify` answers 404. `auth.api.generateOneTimeToken` is undefined, so the plugin is not mounted.
- After, with a scheme registered: generate anonymous answers 401 `UNAUTHORIZED`. Signed in, it answers 400 `Client requests are disabled`. Verify with a bogus token answers 400 `Invalid token`. The hand-off round trip, interception refusal, replay and expiry are as pinned above.
- The vendor dist read: `dist/plugins/one-time-token/index.mjs` has `expiresIn ?? 3` minutes and `storeToken` of `plain`, `hashed`, or `{ type: 'custom-hasher', hash }`. `disableClientRequest` refuses when `c.request` is set. Generate is `GET` behind `sessionMiddleware`, and verify is a `POST` with body `{ token }` that calls `consumeVerificationValue` on `one-time-token:` plus the hash.

</details>

  - the freshness refusal removed: only its stale-session pin went red (1 failed, 36 passed at 4b3e1fd5);
  - the cross-site refusal removed: only its cross-site pin went red (1 failed, 36 passed at 4b3e1fd5);
